titles.title: Thief2
titles.engine: Dark Engine with NewDark 1.26 (Thief2.exe ProductVersion 1.26, log 'App Version: Thief 2 Final 1.26', md5 1109955d4d0a7855592b33d954abcb76, PE subsystem 5.0, MSVCR90 + D3DX9_43). Staged cam_ext.cfg turns on use_d3d_display, force_32bit, single_display_mode 2 and ui_scale_mode 2, so it runs NewDark's Direct3D 9 display at 32 bpp.
titles.launch_sets: 1920x1080x32, fullscreen, on the 1080p LCDs. The mechanism is in the staged tree and correct. 'Play Thief 2.bat' calls FLEETRES.BAT, then runs `FLEETRES.EXE -setline cam.cfg game_screen_size game_screen_size %FR_W% %FR_H%`. The staged FLEETRES.EXE has md5 bb180f3b..., the same as the repo build. Running stage-fleetres.py --check from origin/master c4e5194 reported '216 already current, 0 failures'. GAMESYNC also writes the same line through the GAMERES rule at gameres.h:764 { Thief2, GR_OP_SETLINE, cam.cfg, game_screen_size, 'game_screen_size %W% %H%' }. Measured 2026-09-29 00:10: the deployed cam.cfg on .123, .145, .195 and .240 reads 'game_screen_size 1920 1080'. Thief2.log shows the setting took effect on .123 (08-31), .195 (09-04) and .240 (08-31): 'D3DProvider StartMode: smode 1920x1080x32' and 'CreateDevice: res = D3D_OK ; 1920x1080 ... fs=1'. .145's only log is from 08-30 01:57, before cam.cfg changed, and shows smode 800x600x32. .145, .195 and .240 still have the older 1658-byte launcher; it has the same FLEETRES line and differs only in the vcr-kmd D3D32/BigTex check, so resolution is not affected.
titles.menu_source: The list is the modes the driver reports, intersected with NewDark's hardcoded 159-entry grd_mode_info table (Thief2.exe .data 0x786768, 12-byte entries). That table contains 1920x1080x16 (id 105) and 1920x1080x32 (id 141, widescreen flag 0x80, which adds a ' / <aspect>' label suffix through 0x4521e0). Table strings include '...1920x1200x32 1920x1080x32 1440x1080x32 1680x1050x32 1600x900x32...'. The Options list builder (0x452479) uses the 3D device's mode list. It keeps depth 16 or 32 (only 32 when force_32bit is set), w >= 0x190 (400) and 0x12c (300) <= h <= 0x12c0 (4800), up to 0x40 (64) rows. The NewDark 1.19 release notes in the tree say 'Added ingame support for all common resolutions, including widescreen'. Driver modes that are not in the table are dropped; the log shows 'unsupported mode 1600 x 1024 x 16 (not in mode table)' on .145 and 1152x648 and 1776x1000 on .195. On all four LCD boxes the logged adapter mode list includes '1920 x 1080 x 16' and '1920 x 1080 x 32'.

titles.fix_risk: No change proposed. Watch .240's EDID. The brief says that at about 23:40 its GAMERES reported no EDID and a 1024x768 desktop. My probe at 00:08 read DELL E2313H, LCD, persisted 1920x1080. With no EDID, FLEETRES and GAMERES take the 4:3-tube branch capped at the persisted desktop, so a launch during an EDID dropout would get a 4:3 mode. That is a box fault, not a tree fault.
titles.hw_check: On each LCD box: `EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\Thief2" "Play Thief 2.bat"`. After about 20 s, DOWNLOAD C:\Games\Thief2\Thief2.log (it is rewritten every launch) and require 'game_screen_size 1920 1080', 'D3DProvider StartMode: smode 1920x1080x32' and 'CreateDevice: res = D3D_OK ; 1920x1080 ... fs=1'. Test .145 first: it has no log since cam.cfg changed. In-game menu: Main menu (New Game/Load Game/Options/Credits/Intro/Quit) -> Options -> Video page -> resolution selector must offer 1920x1080x32. The menus follow the absolute Windows cursor (the agent drove New Game -> mission on .124 on 2026-09-28), so UICLICK works. Esc backs out and the mouse wheel scrolls. With ui_scale_mode 2 the 640x480 UI is drawn pillarboxed, so screen = (240 + 2.25x, 2.25y). XP boxes (.123 .145 .240): SCREENSHOT 0 captures the fullscreen D3D9 surface. .195 is Win7, where GDI cannot capture exclusive fullscreen: use Thief2.log and WINLIST, and if a menu picture is required, add force_windowed to cam_ext.cfg as a tool and then remove it. Quit from the menu and confirm DISPLAYCFG get is back at 1920x1080.

titles.title: ThiefGold
titles.engine: Dark Engine, vanilla, no NewDark. THIEF.EXE ProductVersion 1.37, md5 8dd515df75176bcd1caaf65a93f47d81, PE subsystem 4.0. Sections .text/lgalloc/.rdata/.data/.rsrc, with no stxt* section and no SafeDisc. There is no D3DX9_43.dll, NVScript.osm or cam_ext.cfg in the tree (checked case-insensitively).
titles.launch_sets: 640x480 on every LCD box, and no mechanism exists to change it. 'Play Thief Gold.bat' is just `cd /d "%~dp0"` + `start "" thief.exe`: no FLEETRES.BAT or .EXE is staged, gameres.h has no ThiefGold rule, and CAM.CFG and USER.CFG have no game_screen_size line. The engine starts from the static game ScrnMode that 0x4108d0 returns (&0x5e1a40 = {flags 7, 640, 480, 8, 13}). The config reader 0x43b190 overrides it only when it finds 'game_' + 'screen_size' with two ints. The deployed CAM.CFG on .123, .145, .195 and .240 is byte-identical to the staged file (md5 68f695ec...). The 2026-08-31 perbox sweep recorded 640x480 fullscreen on .123, .240 and .246, but those frames are the intro movie. PER-TITLE-STATUS.md says 'incapable, vanilla Dark is 640x480 with no cvar'. That is imprecise: vanilla does read game_screen_size and can set any mode in its fixed table, up to 1600x1200.
titles.menu_source: A hardcoded table. The LG dev2d grd_mode_info table (THIEF.EXE .data 0x615f44, 87 twelve-byte entries) holds 320x200 through 640x480, 800x600, 1024x768, 1280x1024 and 1600x1200 at 4/8/15/16/24/32 bpp, plus 400x300 and 512x384. It has no widescreen entry and no 1920x1080. The Options -> Video list builder (0x51d0b7) draws candidates from the 3D device's mode list in hardware mode, or from the static list at 0x611df0 in software mode (ids [77,78,19,20,21] = 400x300x8, 512x384x8, 640x400x8, 640x480x8, 800x600x8). It keeps only bpp == 16 (hardware) or 8 (software), w >= 0x190 (400) and 0x12c (300) <= h <= 0x300 (768), at most 0xc (12) rows. The in-menu ceiling is therefore 1024x768x16. Outside the menu, game_screen_size can only name a table mode: the lookup at 0x535be0 scans 0x57 (87) entries and returns -1 for anything else. 1920x1080, 1280x960, 1152x864 and 1440x1080 are all absent. Thief 2's 1.18 exe in Thief2/backup has the same 87-entry table and a menu height cap of 0x4b0 (1200), for comparison.

titles.fix: Replace the engine with NewDark for Thief 1/Gold, then treat the title exactly like Thief2. Install NewDark 1.27, which web sources say still runs on XP, over a copy of the staged 1.37 tree in the XP build VM. Use either TFix 1.27d with only the NewDark/engine components selected, or the bare T1 NewDark 1.27 package from TTLG. Then: (1) add ThiefGold to scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py with the same `-setline cam.cfg game_screen_size game_screen_size %FR_W% %FR_H%` line and the vcr-kmd DX6 swap block; (2) add a matching gameres.h GR_OP_SETLINE rule; (3) ship a cam_ext.cfg with use_d3d_display, force_32bit, single_display_mode 2 and ui_scale_mode 2; (4) ship msvcr90.dll, msvcp90.dll, Microsoft.VC90.CRT.manifest and D3DX9_43.dll as Thief2's tree does. NewDark's table has 1920x1080 and its menu lists it. Without new files nothing reaches 1080p. The best vanilla result on these panels is `game_screen_size 1024 768`, the largest 4:3 mode in the vanilla table. FLEETRES's FR_W43 target (1280x960) is not in that table and must not be written.
titles.fix_source: Would need downloading: TFix 1.27d (moddb.com/mods/tfix) or NewDark T1 1.27 (ttlg.com). It is not on the share: a case-insensitive find over Files/, Utility/, DiskImages/, transmission/ and trashbox/ for *newdark*, *tfix*, *t2fix* and *thief* found only the retail 'Thief Gold (1999) - CD1 Install.iso'/'CD2 Game.iso' and Thief_2_The_Metal_Age.rar. That archive holds T2-only NewDark 1.26, and its doc/T1.7z contains only a T1 INTRFACE.CRF and a readme, not an engine. Games/_games_index.json has no other Thief payload.
titles.fix_risk: Saves from 1.37 will not load under NewDark. NewDark drops the software renderer and needs Direct3D, the VC2008 runtime and D3DX9_43. .243 (Win98, no 3D) is already gated for this title. On vcr-kmd (.124) it needs the same cam_ext.cfg DX6 swap Thief II uses. Thief has no multiplayer, so there is no MP or anti-cheat consequence. The NewDark exe keeps the name thief.exe, so launch.txt and the icon still resolve. GAMESYNC never deletes, so old files remain on boxes. CAM.CFG already has skip_starting_checks for the disc probe. Vanilla fallback risk: a game_screen_size that is not in the table has no mode id (the lookup returns -1). What the engine does then is untested; it may end in the 'video hardware is not supported' path. Also, a resolution chosen in the menu on a box is saved into its cfg and can be reverted by a later GAMESYNC of the title.

titles.title: SystemShock2
titles.engine: Dark Engine, vanilla retail 1.0. The tree is a copy of the CD's SHOCK\ folder. shock2.exe is the SafeDisc 1.11.000 v1 loader (ProductVersion 1.15, sections .txt/.text/.txt2). The engine itself is SHOCK2.ICD, which is encrypted (READ-ME-FIRST.txt: 7.88 bits/byte). No NewDark and no official 2.x patch is present.
titles.launch_sets: 640x480 when it runs, but on the LCD boxes it currently does not reach the game at all. .123: no mounter; mount-error.txt reads 'NO DISC MOUNTER IS INSTALLED' and the gate suppresses the shortcut. .240, 08-31 frame: DAEMON Tools 'Unable to mount image. Cue sheet: Unit is locked.' .195 (then .246), 08-31 frame: SafeDisc 'Cannot locate the CD-ROM' over the Xerxes splash, with WinCDEmu. .145: install.reg's own note records a WER crash on 08-30; compat lists it as untested. There is no resolution mechanism. The generated mount launcher's FLEETRES slot is empty (provisioning/discmount/specs/SystemShock2.json has fleetres_block ''), gameres.h has no rule, cam.cfg (the CD copy, md5 fc1bf665..., identical on all four boxes) has no game_screen_size, and shock.cfg says 'screen_size 640,480'. The fleetbook compat_render rows 'verified d3d 1920x1080 fullscreen' for .240 and .246 (perbox, 2026-08-31) are false. Their screenshots show the 1920x1080 desktop with the mount or SafeDisc error dialog, not the game.
titles.menu_source: A hardcoded table, inferred from the unencrypted System Shock 2 demo engine because the retail engine is encrypted. The demo is Files/Games/Demos & Shareware/SystemShock2Demo.exe -> shock/shock2.exe, dated 1999-07-21, and its cam.cfg has the same 'cam.cfg 1.17 1999/06/28' header as the staged tree. It has the same 87-entry grd_mode_info table as Thief Gold: max 1600x1200, no widescreen, no 1920x1080, and the lookup at 0x59e2b0 is `cmp eax,0x57`. Its Options -> Video list builder (0x5629d0) keeps depth-matched modes with w >= 0x280 (640) and 0x1e0 (480) <= h <= 0x300 (768), at most 12 rows. So the menu can show only 640x480, 800x600 and 1024x768.

titles.fix: Install SS2 NewDark 2.48 with SS2Tool. Web sources say SS2Tool supports the retail CD 'shock' folder, which is exactly this tree. It replaces the SafeDisc loader and ICD with an unprotected NewDark engine. That engine family's table includes 1920x1080, as Thief2's 1.26 does, and it also removes the disc image, DAEMON Tools and secdrv dependency that currently stops SS2 on all four LCD boxes. Then: (1) remove disc_mount from requires.json; (2) regenerate or replace the mount launcher from its spec, not by hand-editing, as a plain launcher carrying Thief2's FLEETRES `-setline cam.cfg game_screen_size game_screen_size %FR_W% %FR_H%` line and the vcr-kmd DX6 swap; (3) add a gameres.h GR_OP_SETLINE rule; (4) add cam_ext.cfg with use_d3d_display, force_32bit, single_display_mode 2 and ui_scale_mode 2. Without new files the only change is `game_screen_size 1024 768` in cam.cfg, the vanilla table's largest 4:3 mode. That is still 4:3 and still needs the disc to start.
titles.fix_source: Would need downloading: SS2Tool v6.x (systemshock.org topic 4141, or a mirror such as gamepressure), which fetches NewDark 2.48. Web sources say SS2Tool itself needs Vista or later, while NewDark runs on 2000/XP. So run SS2Tool against a copy of the staged tree on the Linux host under Wine or on a Vista+ VM, not on a fleet box, or apply the bare NewDark 2.48 package by hand in the XP build VM. It is not on the share: a case-insensitive find for *ss2tool*, *newdark* and *shock* found only disc images (System_Shock_2.zip, System_Shock_2_(1999).zip, 'System Shock 2 (1999)/*.bin/.cue', the Multiplayer copy), System_Shock_Enhanced_v1.6.7z (which is System Shock 1) and the 74 MB demo.
titles.fix_risk: Saves from 1.0 do not carry over. SS2Tool also applies the 2.x content patch and optional community fixes, so select only the engine and vanilla fixes. NewDark SS2 brings back co-op multiplayer; every box must carry the same build, and there is no anti-cheat. The software renderer is dropped. vcr-kmd (.124) needs the DX6 cam_ext.cfg swap. install.reg's secdrv Start=2 and AppCompatFlags GUID become obsolete but harmless. GAMESYNC never deletes, so SHOCK2.ICD and the 650 MB _disc image stay on boxes unless the launcher removes them. Check the new exe's PE subsystem is 5.x or lower for XP.

titles.title: JediKnightDF2
titles.engine: Sith engine. JK.EXE is 1.01 (FileVersion 1,0,1,0, md5 85f8f883bbb7a167429879c899be1803), from the GOG tree with its ogg winmm.dll music wrapper. It uses DirectDraw plus Direct3D (DX5 immediate mode), with an 8-bit software renderer and 16-bit 3D.
titles.launch_sets: 640x480 with the 8-bpp software renderer on all four LCD boxes, and nothing in the staged tree sets a mode. launch.txt runs JK.EXE directly: no FLEETRES, no gameres rule, and install.reg sets only CD Path and InstallType. The mode lives in HKLM\SOFTWARE\LucasArts Entertainment Company\JediKnight\v1.0 as displayMode (an index into this box's DirectDraw mode array) plus b3DAccel. It is written only when Setup -> Display is closed with OK (0x414c1e). REGREAD at 2026-09-29 00:08 on .123, .145, .195 and .240 shows only CD Path, InstallType and Version=0.1, so it has never been saved on any of them. JK therefore uses its default: FindClosestMode(640x480) (0x4146b3..0x4146e8, ERR_NEED_256_COLOR if that mode is not 8 bpp) with b3DAccel 0. The 08-31 perbox sweep recorded 640x480 fullscreen.
titles.menu_source: The list comes from the driver, not a table. stdDisplay calls IDirectDraw::EnumDisplayModes with flags 0 twice (0x425bb2). The first pass, under DDSCL_NORMAL, uses callback 0x426030 and keeps only 320-wide ModeX modes. The second, under DDSCL_EXCLUSIVE|FULLSCREEN, uses callback 0x425e30 and keeps every mode. Both fill one 84-byte-stride array at 0x866cc0 with a hard cap of 0x40 = 64 modes (`cmp edi,0x40; jae`). Setup -> Display -> 'Video Modes' (0x4150c0) shows every stored mode whose bpp is 16 when '3D Acceleration' is ticked, or 8 when it is not. There is no width or height filter, and entries are labelled L"%dx%d %dbpp %s". So '1920x1080 16bpp' appears whenever DirectDraw reports it among the first 64 modes. The drivers do offer 1920x1080 at 16 bpp: NewDark's R5G6B5 enumeration in Thief2.log lists 1920 x 1080 x 16 on all four boxes. The 64-slot count, using GAMERES resolution counts times up to three depths: .123 15 -> 45, .145 16 -> 48, .195 20 -> 60, which always fits. .240 has 24 -> 72, plus its 320x200 and 320x240 first-pass entries, which is over 64, so it depends on DirectDraw's enumeration order and is UNKNOWN on .240. PER-TITLE-STATUS.md calls this title 'incapable - index into a list the 3D device supplies; no widescreen entry'. That is wrong.

titles.fix: None needed for the in-game option to exist; that is true on .123, .145 and .195, and needs checking on .240. To make the title start at 1080p, each box needs a displayMode index and b3DAccel=1 in HKLM. This cannot go in install.reg, because the index points into each box's own DirectDraw enumeration. The simplest route is one pass per box through Setup -> Display: tick 3D Acceleration, pick '1920x1080 16bpp', press OK. The value persists, since install.reg never touches it. The automated route would be a new FLEETRES mode that reproduces JK's two-pass, 64-slot EnumDisplayModes to compute the index; that does not exist today. If .240 overflows the 64 slots, nothing in the tree can fix it.
titles.fix_source: already in tree (the engine offers the mode); nothing to download
titles.fix_risk: Resolution is client-local, so DirectPlay peer multiplayer (LAN proof on .123 + .240, 2026-08-31) is unaffected, and there is no anti-cheat. Pressing OK writes to HKLM; on Win7 (.195) UAC may redirect that to VirtualStore. 16-bit Direct3D at 1920x1080 has not been run on these cards yet; the largest mode proven is 1280x960x16 on .124. The Sith engine was built for 4:3, so check the widescreen image for stretching or vert- cropping in game.
titles.hw_check: `EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\JediKnightDF2" JK.EXE`, press Esc past the intro. The GUI switches the display to 640x480, so UICLICK uses 640x480 coordinates. The mouse follows the absolute cursor; the 2026-08-31 LAN proof drove Host and Join through the agent. Keyboard navigation is unverified. Path: Main menu -> Setup -> Display tab -> tick '3D Acceleration' -> scroll the 'Video Modes' list and look for '1920x1080 16bpp'. DF2's GUI is 8-bit, so SCREENSHOT comes back nearly black (README-FLEET). Read the list on MotS first, or pick the mode and press OK, then REGREAD HKLM\SOFTWARE\LucasArts Entertainment Company\JediKnight\v1.0 (displayMode and b3DAccel should now exist), start a level, and require DISPLAYCFG get or WINLIST to show 1920x1080 in game. During a verification-only pass press Cancel instead of OK. On .240, specifically confirm the list reaches 1920x1080, because of the 64-mode cap.

The alternative is a future FLEETRES mode that replicates the 64-slot enumeration. A staged index would be wrong on other boxes by construction.

titles.fix_risk: Same as DF2. The resolution is client-local, so DirectPlay peer multiplayer (LAN proof .123 + .240) is unaffected and there is no anti-cheat. On Win7 (.195) UAC may redirect the HKLM write to VirtualStore. 16-bit 3D at 1920x1080 has not been exercised on these cards.
titles.hw_check: `EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\JediKnightMotS" JKM.EXE`, press Esc past the intros. Path: Main menu -> Setup -> Display tab -> tick '3D Acceleration' -> 'Video Modes' list must contain '1920x1080 16bpp'. MotS menus are 16-bit, so SCREENSHOT 0 captures the list on XP (.123 .145 .240); this is the better title for photographing the Sith list. The GUI runs at 640x480, so UICLICK uses 640x480 coordinates with the absolute cursor; the LAN proof drove these menus through the agent. On .195 (Win7) use REGREAD and DISPLAYCFG get or WINLIST instead of pictures. For a fullscreen proof: select the mode, press OK, start a level, confirm DISPLAYCFG get or WINLIST reads 1920x1080 in game, then REGREAD the MotS key. During verification-only work press Cancel. Check .240 explicitly for the 64-mode cap.
